title: Verification of Forecasts Expressed in Terms of Probability
abstract: Foundational paper introducing a proper quadratic score for evaluating probabilistic forecasts, later known as the Brier score; directly relevant to empirical reliability and calibration evaluation.

title: A Coefficient of Agreement for Nominal Scales
abstract: Introduces Cohen's kappa for measuring agreement between two raters while accounting for agreement expected by chance, providing a foundation for annotation-reliability assessment.

title: On Optimum Recognition Error and Reject Tradeoff
abstract: Develops the classical decision-theoretic tradeoff between recognition error and rejection, foundational for selective prediction and abstention under asymmetric costs.

title: Evaluating Content Selection in Summarization: The Pyramid Method
abstract: Introduces an empirically grounded method for evaluating summary content selection by weighting semantic content units according to how many human reference summaries contain them, yielding an explicit denominator for coverage.

title: Computing Reliability for Coreference Annotation
abstract: Develops a reliability methodology for structured linguistic annotation where disagreements can be partial and annotation units are not trivially commensurate.

title: The Pyramid Method: Incorporating human content selection variation in summarization evaluation
venue: ACM Transactions on Speech and Language Processing
abstract: Extends the Pyramid Method for summary-content evaluation by explicitly representing variation among human summaries and using weighted semantic content units to assess content coverage.

title: A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction
abstract: Tutorial treatment of conformal prediction and its coverage guarantees under exchangeability assumptions; useful as a foundation for statistically controlled abstention and uncertainty sets.

title: Formal and functional assessment of the pyramid method for summary content evaluation
abstract: Evaluates the reliability and discriminative power of Pyramid annotations across multiple summarization evaluations, including inter-annotator reliability and consistency of system rankings.

title: PEAK: Pyramid Evaluation via Automated Knowledge Extraction
abstract: Automates Pyramid-style summary-content evaluation using extracted knowledge representations, retaining the idea of evaluating semantic information units rather than lexical overlap alone.

title: Runtime Verification of Temporal Properties over Out-of-order Data Streams
abstract: Studies verification of temporal properties when observations arrive out of order, providing transferable machinery for reasoning about changing state and late evidence in event streams.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Studies selective classification in which a model may reject inputs, emphasizing the risk-coverage tradeoff and methods for attaining a desired error risk at useful coverage.

title: Know What You Don't Know: Unanswerable Questions for SQuAD
abstract: Introduces SQuAD 2.0, combining answerable and adversarially written unanswerable questions so systems must determine when the supplied passage does not support an answer and abstain.

title: FEVER: a large-scale dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification
abstract: Introduces claim verification against textual sources with Supported, Refuted, and NotEnoughInfo labels; supporting or refuting judgments also include the source sentences necessary as evidence.

title: Can You Trust Your Model's Uncertainty? Evaluating Predictive Uncertainty Under Dataset Shift
abstract: Systematically evaluates predictive uncertainty and calibration under dataset shift, showing that uncertainty quality can deteriorate as inputs move away from the training distribution.

title: SelectiveNet: A Deep Neural Network with an Integrated Reject Option
abstract: Integrates prediction and selection into a single model trained to achieve a target coverage while minimizing selective risk, making coverage an explicit constraint rather than rewarding indiscriminate rejection.

title: Agreement is overrated: A plea for correlation to assess human evaluation reliability
abstract: Examines reliability assessment in NLG human evaluation and argues that inter-annotator agreement alone can be misleading; recommends considering agreement together with correlation measures.

title: Evaluating the Factual Consistency of Abstractive Text Summarization
abstract: Introduces a source-grounded factual-consistency model that jointly predicts consistency and extracts a supporting source span and an inconsistent summary span, enabling localized evidence for factuality judgments.

title: On Faithfulness and Factuality in Abstractive Summarization
abstract: Uses large-scale human evaluation to characterize hallucinations in abstractive summaries and compares automatic measures, finding textual-entailment measures more informative about source faithfulness than standard overlap metrics.

title: Asking and Answering Questions to Evaluate the Factual Consistency of Summaries
abstract: Introduces QAGS, which generates questions from a summary and compares answers obtained from the summary and source; disagreement exposes factual inconsistency and gives interpretable question-answer evidence.

title: Evaluating Factuality in Generation with Dependency-level Entailment
abstract: Evaluates factuality at a finer granularity than whole sentences by predicting entailment of dependency-level semantic relations against source documents, helping localize factual errors.

title: Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims
abstract: Introduces SciFact, where systems retrieve scientific abstracts, determine whether evidence supports or refutes a claim, and identify rationale spans justifying the decision.

title: Selective Question Answering under Domain Shift
abstract: Defines selective QA under domain shift, requiring systems to answer as many questions as possible while maintaining a specified accuracy; demonstrates that raw model probabilities are inadequate and evaluates calibrated abstention by coverage.

title: Factual Consistency Evaluation for Text Summarization via Counterfactual Estimation
abstract: Proposes source-grounded factual-consistency evaluation based on counterfactual estimation, targeting whether information in a generated summary is supported by its source.

title: The Art of Abstention: Selective Prediction and Error Regularization for Natural Language Processing
abstract: Studies selective prediction across NLP tasks and evaluates confidence estimators for abstention, adding error regularization intended to improve separation of correct from incorrect predictions.

title: QuestEval: Summarization Asks for Fact-based Evaluation
abstract: Uses question generation and question answering over source and summary to evaluate whether generated text preserves relevant source information and remains factually consistent.

title: How Can We Know When Language Models Know? On the Calibration of Language Models for Question Answering
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
abstract: Studies whether language-model probabilities in question answering correspond to empirical correctness and investigates techniques for improving confidence calibration.

title: Human evaluation of automatically generated text: Current trends and best practice guidelines
abstract: Reviews human-evaluation practice in NLG and provides guidelines covering study design, execution, reporting, reliability, and reproducibility.

title: Classification with Rejection Based on Cost-sensitive Classification
abstract: Connects classification with rejection to cost-sensitive classification and develops a theoretically justified reject-option method applicable to binary and multiclass settings.

title: SummEval: Re-evaluating Summarization Evaluation
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
abstract: Provides a large meta-evaluation of summarization metrics using both expert and crowdsourced human judgments, creating a common testbed for factual consistency and other evaluation dimensions.

title: SummaC: Re-Visiting NLI-based Models for Inconsistency Detection in Summarization
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
abstract: Revisits natural-language-inference approaches to detecting whether summaries contain statements unsupported by their source documents and meta-evaluates them across factual-consistency datasets.

title: QAFactEval: Improved QA-Based Factual Consistency Evaluation for Summarization
abstract: Improves question-answering-based factual consistency evaluation by systematically selecting and combining QA components for testing whether summary claims are supported by source documents.

title: TRUE: Re-evaluating Factual Consistency Evaluation
abstract: Constructs a standardized collection of factual-consistency datasets and performs an example-level meta-evaluation of metrics across summarization, dialogue, paraphrasing, and fact verification.

title: Attributed Question Answering: Evaluation and Modeling for Attributed Large Language Models
abstract: Defines attributed question answering, where answers must be accompanied by evidence sources that support them, and develops human and automatic evaluation of answer quality and attribution.

title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
abstract: Decomposes long-form generations into atomic facts and measures factual precision as the proportion of atomic claims supported by a designated knowledge source, enabling claim-level verification.

title: AlignScore: Evaluating Factual Consistency with A Unified Alignment Function
abstract: Learns a unified text-alignment function for source-grounded factual-consistency evaluation and evaluates it across multiple factuality and information-alignment tasks.

title: Revisiting the Gold Standard: Grounding Summarization Evaluation with Robust Human Evaluation
abstract: Introduces robust human evaluation based on Atomic Content Units and the RoSE benchmark, explicitly measuring semantic content coverage with fine-grained units and reporting annotator reliability.

title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
abstract: Introduces ALCE for long-form generation with citations and evaluates citation quality, including whether cited passages entail generated claims and whether claims that require support are adequately cited.

title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Introduces a reference-free evaluation framework for RAG pipelines with separate dimensions for retrieval relevance, use of retrieved context, and faithfulness of generated answers to that context.

title: Conformal Risk Control
abstract: Extends conformal methodology from set coverage to controlling expected values of general monotone loss functions, with applications including language and question-answering losses.

title: ACUEval: Fine-grained Hallucination Evaluation and Correction for Abstractive Summarization
abstract: Decomposes summaries into atomic content units and checks individual units against source text, enabling fine-grained hallucination detection rather than a single whole-summary faithfulness score.

title: On the Role of Summary Content Units in Text Summarization Evaluation
abstract: Studies semantic summary-content units as the basic objects of evaluation and compares different unit definitions and annotation approaches for content-oriented summarization assessment.

title: On the Capacity of Citation Generation by Large Language Models
abstract: Investigates LLM citation-generation capability and evaluates generated citations for qualities beyond mere citation presence, including their relationship to the claims they are intended to support.

title: Learning Fine-Grained Grounded Citations for Attributed Large Language Models
abstract: Studies fine-grained citations for attributed generation, aiming to connect generated claims to localized supporting evidence rather than attaching only coarse document-level references.

title: Model Internals-based Answer Attribution for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Introduces an attribution approach for RAG that links answer content to retrieved documents using model internals and evaluates its agreement with human evidence-attribution judgments.

title: Conformal Prediction for Natural Language Processing: A Survey
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
abstract: Surveys conformal prediction in NLP, including assumptions, prediction sets, risk control, structured language outputs, and complications that arise when applying statistical coverage guarantees to language tasks.

title: Better than Random: Reliable NLG Human Evaluation with Constrained Active Sampling
abstract: Studies sampling reliability in NLG human evaluation and proposes constrained active sampling to make limited human-review budgets more representative and stable across system comparisons.

title: Defining and Detecting Vulnerability in Human Evaluation Guidelines: A Preliminary Study Towards Reliable NLG Evaluation
abstract: Investigates how weaknesses or ambiguity in human-evaluation instructions can compromise NLG judgments and develops methodology for identifying evaluation-guideline vulnerabilities.

title: ReproHum #0892-01: The painful route to consistent results: A reproduction study of human evaluation in NLG
abstract: Reproduces an NLG human-evaluation study and analyzes difficulties in obtaining consistent judgments, providing empirical evidence about protocol sensitivity and evaluation reliability.

title: Factual consistency evaluation of summarization in the Era of large language models
abstract: Evaluates source-grounded factual consistency of summaries in the LLM era and studies metric behavior against human factuality judgments, including a clinical summarization setting.

title: Correctness is not Faithfulness in RAG Attributions
abstract: Separates attribution correctness from attribution faithfulness in RAG, showing that a citation can support an answer while failing to reflect the evidence that actually influenced generation.

title: ChronoFact: Timeline-based Temporal Fact Verification
abstract: Frames temporal fact verification around timelines so claims can be evaluated against evidence valid at relevant times, rather than treating factual truth as temporally invariant.

title: SelfCite: Self-Supervised Alignment for Context Attribution in Large Language Models
abstract: Uses context ablations to derive self-supervised citation rewards related to citation necessity and sufficiency, then aligns models to produce better-supported context attributions.

title: Do LLMs Know When to NOT Answer? Investigating Abstention Abilities of Large Language Models
abstract: Systematically evaluates LLM abstention across question-answering settings and introduces abstention-focused evaluation rather than crediting models merely for answering more questions.

title: When Benchmarks Age: Temporal Misalignment through Large Language Model Factuality Evaluation
abstract: Examines temporal misalignment in factuality benchmarks, showing why factuality evaluation must account for benchmark age and whether facts and evidence remain current at evaluation time.

title: Cited but Not Verified: Parsing and Evaluating Source Attribution in LLM Deep Research Agents
abstract: Evaluates source attribution in deep-research outputs by checking whether cited sources work, contain relevant material, and actually substantiate generated factual claims rather than merely appearing plausible.

title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
abstract: Benchmarks LLM citation verifiers against human-reviewed and adjudicated judgments of source relevance and factual support, emphasizing false-positive and false-negative behavior rather than raw judge agreement alone.

title: Do LLMs Know When Evidence is Insufficient? An Evidence Sufficiency Benchmark for Answer-Abstention Calibration in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Benchmarks answer-versus-abstain behavior under full, partial, irrelevant, absent, and conflicting retrieved evidence, directly testing whether RAG systems distinguish insufficient evidence from supported answerability.

title: Agreement Metrics for LLM-as-Judge Evaluation: What to Report and Why
abstract: Analyzes agreement metrics for LLM-as-judge evaluation and discusses what different measures reveal, including treatment of judge abstentions and the need to report coverage alongside agreement.

title: Augmenting Human Evaluation with LLM Judges: How Many Human Reviews Do You Need?
abstract: Studies hybrid evaluation designs that combine LLM judges with retained human review, focusing on how much human validation is needed rather than treating model judgments as an unvalidated gold standard.
